title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
description: Motivation: we observed intermittent request starvation and growing tail latency in the continuous batcher under mixed-priority workloads, especially when short low-cost requests interleave with large long-running decoder requests. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add explicit starvation prevention, and make batch assembly timeouts more deterministic. Summary of changes: bumped scheduler to weighted fair queuing with per-queue aging; add max-wait and priority-decay hooks to prevent indefinite starvation of low-weight queues; introduce adaptive batch-assembly timeout that decays with queue age and observed throughput; surface new metrics for queue_wait_time, queue_starvation_count, and timeout_evictions; make timeouts configurable per-model and per-queue via SchedulerConfig; add unit and integration tests, a perf canary config and a gradual rollout plan behind a feature flag. Implementation notes: replaced simple FIFO windowing with a round-robin WFQ implementation that uses configurable weights and an exponential aging factor to boost starved queues; added a max_wait_ms hard deadline that will force-evict pending items into their own mini-batch to avoid live-lock; implemented a timeout sampler that adjusts assembly_timeout_ms based on recent fill rates and median sample token lengths; moved several hot paths into hot-inlined helpers and reduced atomic contention by using per-worker local queues with a low-overhead steal path. Compatibility and rollout: default behavior is backward-compatible; all new timeout and wfq knobs are behind "continuous_batcher_v2" feature flag; rollout plan: 10% canary on dedicated pools for 48h -> 50% for 24h -> global if metrics stable. Testing and validation: synthetic mixed-priority workload tests show p95 latency drop 12% and starvation_count drop 98% across 1M-request simulation; end-to-end GA perf canary across three clusters shows 8-11% token throughput improvement for small-request-heavy workloads while keeping peak GPU utilization steady. Related: ENG-4821, ENG-4937, PM-1272.
